raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, so I cannot play big games. What keeps my house steady is the usual wheat and maize rotation. If I change too much and one crop goes wrong, that hurts more than saving a little money. So this year I will still do wheat after maize, and maize right after wheat, same as around here. I watch my own field and what the nearby families do. Wheat needs to look strong before winter, so I will put some fertilizer at sowing and then add more when it starts growing fast in spring. Water from the well costs money, but if the land stays dry at wheat sowing, jointing, or filling, I will irrigate. Maize has a tight planting window after wheat harvest, so I will not do heavy tillage. I will clear the wheat, turn the soil lightly, and sow fast. I do not want to spend too much cash at once, so I will buy ordinary wheat seed and a decent hybrid maize seed, then use moderate fertilizer, not the highest. If pests are light, I will not spray much. If they show up, then I spend the money.
